t: A South Indian dynasty that ruled from Kanchipuram for some six centuries, at its height the leading power of the south.
Narasimhavarman I sacked the Chalukya capital Vatapi in 642, during a long rivalry with the Chalukyas of Badami.
Its temples at Mamallapuram and Kanchipuram founded Dravidian architecture, and its script spread across Southeast Asia.
dyk: King Mahendravarman I wrote a Sanskrit comedy in which a drunken Shaiva ascetic accuses a Buddhist monk of stealing his skull begging bowl, which a dog had actually carried off.
ev: Simhavishnu defeats the Kalabhras and extends Pallava rule to the Kaveri
Narasimhavarman I sacks Vatapi; the Chalukya king Pulakeshin II dies
Rajasimha builds the Shore Temple and the Kailasanatha temple
Vikramaditya II of the Chalukyas occupies Kanchipuram
Pallavas and Gangas defeat the Pandyas at Sripurambiyam
Aditya I of the Cholas defeats Aparajita and annexes the kingdom

f.founder: Simhavishnu (founder of the later Pallava line)
